insights.methodology: Every insight cites the specific ratio/period pair it is derived from in ratios_timeseries.json.

risk_signals.statement: CAR has stayed well above the regulatory minimum (12.5%) for every year since FY2018 (13.0%-17.2% range), reaching a series high of 17.2% in FY2020 during COVID-19, and remaining >15% through FY2023. This is among the strongest capital positions of any bank researched so far in this dataset.

NPL ratio jumped sharply from 4.1% (FY2023) to 7.7% (FY2024), the worst level in the full 15-year series (prior range was 2.2%-5.2%), driven by a large increase in loan-loss provisioning to BDT 16,993.3mn in FY2024 (per the FY2025 annual report's own comparative column, Note to the P&L). ROE roughly halved over the same period (17.9% -> 9.17%). This aligns with the broader FY2024 stress seen across several other DSE banks in this dataset (e.g. Dhaka Bank, AB Bank, Al-Arafah Islami Bank). CORRECTION (2026-08-26): this signal previously misattributed the BDT 10,235.2mn figure to FY2023 -- verified against the source text (annual_reports/DUTCHBANGL/dutchbangl-annual-report-2025.txt, line ~6767, 'Total provision 10,235,169,706 | 16,993,298,620'), that figure is FY2025's own total provision (the comparative column pairs it with FY2024's 16,993,298,620), not FY2023's; FY2023's total provision was never extracted into this dataset. See the new 'provisioning_reversal_q4_2025' signal below for what the 10,235.2mn figure actually evidences.

The FY2024 provisioning surge was not evenly spread across the year: cumulative provision_for_loans_cumulative was BDT 1,042.8mn through Q1, jumped to BDT 5,018.6mn by Q2 (a Q2-alone charge of ~3,975.8mn, roughly 4x Q1's pace), reached BDT 9,391.4mn by Q3, and finished the year at BDT 16,993.3mn -- meaning Q4 2024 alone added a further ~7,601.9mn, the single largest quarterly charge of the year. Quarterly granularity (added 2026-08-26) shows the FY2024 asset-quality recognition event was back-loaded and accelerating, not a one-time Q1 reset.

FY2025's full-year total provision (BDT 10,235.2mn, per the annual report) is LOWER than the bank's own cumulative provision_for_loans_cumulative reported through just the first nine months of the same year (BDT 15,414.1mn as of Q3 2025) -- implying a Q4-2025-alone provision reversal/release of approximately BDT -5,178.9mn. This is consistent with, and adds quarter-level evidence for, the already-documented FY2025 recovery (profit after tax more than doubling YoY): cumulative net profit after tax was only BDT 885.1mn through Q1 2025 (EPS 1.01) and BDT 2,557.0mn through Q3 (EPS 2.65), versus BDT 9,647.7mn for the full year (EPS 9.98) -- meaning Q4 2025 alone contributed roughly BDT 7,090.7mn of profit, more than the first three quarters combined, driven substantially by this provision release.

FY2025 shows a sharp one-year recovery: NPL ratio improved from 7.7% to 6.4% (though still above the pre-2024 norm), profit after tax more than doubled (BDT 4,735mn -> 9,648mn), and ROE recovered from 9.17% to 16.06%.

Total assets grew from BDT 123.3bn (FY2011) to BDT 817.8bn (FY2025), a 6.6x increase over 15 years (14.4% CAGR), with growth accelerating notably from FY2019 onward (BDT 390.4bn) as paid-up capital was raised from BDT 2,000mn to BDT 9,667mn across successive rights/bonus issues.

insights.historical_context: Dutch-Bangla Bank shows one of the strongest and most consistent capital-adequacy profiles researched in this dataset, with CAR never dropping below 11% across 15 years and typically well above 13%. Its FY2024 asset-quality shock (NPL more than doubling YoY) followed by a sharp FY2025 recovery mirrors the pattern seen at Dhaka Bank over the same two years, reinforcing that FY2024 was a broadly difficult year across the sector rather than a bank-specific event.

sources.note: 45 of a possible 48 quarters extracted (2010 Q1 through 2026 Q2; 2026 is a bonus partial year beyond this dataset's existing Q4/annual terminal year of 2025, included because it was genuinely available). Format splits exactly as the prior research pass anticipated: 2015 onward is one combined PDF per quarter (Balance Sheet + P&L + Cash Flow + Statement of Changes in Equity); 2010-2014 is a static .htm landing page per quarter linking 1-3 separate PDFs (Balance Sheet, Profit & Loss, sometimes Cash Flow/Statement of Changes in Equity as their own files; 2011/2012 Q1/Q3 and 2014 Q2 instead link one already-combined PDF). Confirmed gaps, not backfilled: 2011 Q2 (the site's own Q2-2011 link points to a generic price-sensitive-information page, not a report; no Wayback capture of any PDF exists under Interim_Report/2011_second_quarter/); 2013 Q2 and Q3 (never published in this format -- confirmed absent from a 2015-04-06 Wayback capture of the same listing page, not just a dead link); 2016 Q3 (the site's own link, Interim_Report/2016_third_quarter/Financial_Statements_30_September_2016.pdf, 404s live and has no successful Wayback capture at any timestamp, despite the FY2016 annual report itself confirming a Q3 statement was released 30 October 2016 -- the PDF is simply not recoverable from any source checked). 2014 Q1 was downloaded and OCR'd but excluded from bank_financials/DUTCHBANGL/quarterly/ entirely: OCR quality on the 85 PPI source scan was insufficient for confident headline-total extraction even after 8x upscaling (see annual_reports/DUTCHBANGL/dutchbangl-interim-2014-q1-*.txt for the retained OCR attempt). 2020 Q3's PDF is delisted from the live page (a dead link) but still resolves at its original URL and was used after confirming via its own comparative column that it is a genuine DBBL filing. Reporting convention: Q1 and Q2 filings are titled 'First Quarter'/'Half-Yearly'; Q3 filings show both a 9-month-cumulative and a discrete-3-month column -- the 9-month CUMULATIVE column was used throughout for income-statement items (never the discrete quarter), matching the convention already established for CITYBANK and matching how this bank's own Q4 = Annual-minus-9M derivation in _methodology.md expects Q1-Q3 to be stored. Two format quirks found and handled: (1) 2015-2017 balance sheets are printed as 'Main Operation and Off-shore Banking Unit' in three columns; the Main-Operation-only column was used throughout, consistent with this dataset's existing FY2016 Q4 precedent (see that period_note) which rejected the combined Main+OBU figure for the same reason. (2) 2018-2019 interim filings title their statements 'Consolidated Balance Sheet'/'Consolidated Profit and Loss Account' with no separate solo statement in the document -- flagged per project convention, though every comparative column checked reconciles exactly with this dataset's existing solo-basis annual figures for the same dates, so there is no evidence of an actual consolidation-scope difference, only a label change specific to that vintage of the report template. PDFs from 2024 Q1 onward (plus 2020 Q3, and 2012 Q2/2013 Q1/2014 Q1 from the old era) had no extractable text layer (confirmed via pdffonts/pdfimages -- either a pure scanned image or a font with no ToUnicode map) and were OCR'd (pdftoppm 300-400 DPI + tesseract, upscaled 6-8x for the lowest-resolution old scans); every OCR'd quarter's headline figures were cross-validated against the balance-sheet identity, the operating-income/PBT/PAT subtotal identities, and (where a later report's comparative column covered the same date) a second independent source, before being accepted -- two OCR misreads were caught and corrected this way (2025 Q1's 'Total operating income' and EPS). 2013 Q1 is flagged as lower-confidence in its own quarterly/2013_Q1.json: its balance sheet reconciles and cross-checks against a later report's comparative column, but its P&L subtotals were mostly illegible and were reconstructed from individually-legible line items with no second source to check against.
